subject: general
question: Name the gas which is filled in wick-type lighters.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Butane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wick-Type Lighters **

 
 
• A spark wheel** inside the Zippo is spun against flint **to operate wick-type lighters.
 
• This **generates a spark that lights wick fluid**.
 
• As a fuel, it uses the liquefied petroleum gas** butane**.
 
• Other lighters, such as **cigarette lighters, include a reservoir of lighter fluid**, a valve, and an ignition device in addition to a liquefied flammable gas like **propane or butane**.
 
 
 
• **Butane**
 
 
• Butane is a hydrocarbon that can be easily liquefied and is a highly **flammable, colourless, and odourless gas**.
 
• It is frequently employed as a fuel for **portable stoves and cigarette lighters, as a propellant in aerosols, as a heating fuel, as a refrigerant, and in the production of a wide variety of goods**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Helium**

 
 
• It is the **first member of the noble gas group** in the periodic table and is a **colourless, odourless, tasteless, non-toxic, inert, and monatomic gas**.
 
• Helium is used in a variety of applications, including cryogenic research, arc welding, refrigeration, aircraft gas, nuclear reactor coolant, and gas leak detection.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen **
 
 
• Approximately **80% of the air** we breathe is made up of nitrogen gas.
 
• In the **chemical industry**, nitrogen is crucial. In addition to** nylon, nitric acid, dyes, and explosives, it is used to make fertilizers**. 
 
• It is also used to **preserve food**.
 
 
 
• **Methane**
 
 
• A** flammable, colourless, and odourless** gas is methane.
 
• It serves primarily as a **fuel for producing heat and light**. 
 
• In landfills, marshes, septic tanks, and sewers, **methane is a common byproduct of the decomposition of organic materials**.
